Human capital in abundance, universities and research of an international level, a dynamic research ecosystem, innovative supply chains and a growing vocation for sustainability. Assets which, however, still produce limited results in the area, with wide margins for improvement for example in the patenting and start-up fields, for a territory called to face some decisive challenges to transform its potential into stable and widespread growth: retaining talent, supporting the development of new businesses, strengthening strategic infrastructures.

This is the picture of Pavia that emerges from Assolombarda's analysis, exposed in the 'Your Next Pavia' event, which brought together institutions, businesses, universities and local stakeholders to discuss the development prospects of the province. Furthermore, it is an opportunity to present the update of the 'Strategic plan for the relaunch of the Pavia area' and the first 'Report on the Pavia innovation ecosystem', created by the Assolombarda Study Centre.

A report that highlights some of the area's strengths, such as the over 30,000 enrolled at the University and at the University Institute of Higher Studies, a rapidly expanding audience in recent years (+17.2% between 2019/2020 and 2024/2025) and concentrated in high quality profile courses, with doctorates doubled in six years, with today more than 1,300 enrolled. Potential only partially exploited, because many of the graduates trained locally do not stop here to live and work. In Pavia, in fact, the percentage of graduates between 25 and 39 years old is equal to 25.3% in 2024, a share clearly lower than the Lombard average (34.4%) and also the national average (30.9%). Furthermore, as of 2025, almost 43 thousand citizens of the province are registered in the Registry Office abroad, with a rather high incidence compared to the resident population of 7.9%: 23% are between 18 and 34 years old and, above all, 26% are between 35 and 49 years old. And if Pavia occupies a significant position in terms of scientific production and ability to attract EU funds, it is instead behind in terms of patent intensity and start-ups, in both cases worth less than 2% of the Lombardy total.

«Today - explains the president of Assolombarda Alvise Biffi - we are facing a phase of profound global transformations, marked by geopolitical tensions and a particularly complex economic scenario, which directly impacts businesses and their growth prospects. In this context, companies are demonstrating the ability to adapt, strategic vision and willingness to invest in innovation as a development lever. It is in this direction that Assolombarda continues to work in its quadrilateral formed by Milan, Monza and Brianza, Lodi and Pavia, strengthening collaboration between companies, universities and institutions and promoting projects capable of accompanying industrial transformation. These include forgIA, the project with which we want to bring Artificial Intelligence into manufacturing through the creation of a shared, secure and interoperable digital ecosystem. At the same time, we are working to expand the internationalization opportunities of companies and open new strategic development corridors. In this path, the Pavia area plays a central role: the success of the first Pavia Innovation Week, the strengthening of the Microelectronics District and the Fostering Chips project demonstrate the vitality of a future-oriented entrepreneurial and scientific ecosystem. Today more than ever, innovation, international openness and skills are the indispensable conditions for supporting the competitiveness of our production system."

The Report presented is part of the path started by Assolombarda in 2020 with the 'Strategic Plan for the relaunch of the Pavia area', of which the update, the results achieved and the new projects were presented today. The Plan identifies four strategic directions - Innovation, Human Capital, Sustainability and Corporate Culture - and three territorial focuses dedicated to Oltrepò, Vigevano and Lomellina, through a program divided into 15 projects aimed at strengthening the competitiveness, attractiveness and cohesion of the territory.
